title: IdTokenClaims
description: The claim set of an ID token, derived from identity_oidc::jwt::IdTokenClaims. This is the payload half of a JWS: the header half is JwtHeader (jwt-header.schema.json), and the signature is never produced by identity-oidc — that is identity-security's job, and the crate is not allowed to depend on it. Every registered claim is required; the profile and email claims are present only when the corresponding scope was granted, which is what Option means here.
x-serde-status: the type is IMPLEMENTED as a shape; no ID token is signed anywhere in the bootstrap phase — signing is DEFERRED to phase 4 (OIDC provider)
x-not-yet-producible: identity-oidc can serialise this claim set and can check is_expired_at, and can do NOTHING else: no signing, no verification, no signature checking, no issuer or audience check. A claim set that validates as a token is not a valid token.

iss.description: The issuer. Must equal the discovery document's 'issuer' exactly, including scheme and any trailing slash. It is an opaque identifier that happens to look like a URL, not a URL the provider resolves.

sub.description: The subject — the user. The same string across every client, per subject_types_supported == ["public"].

aud.description: The audience: the client the token was minted for. A String in Rust, not an array — this provider mints a token for exactly one client.

exp.description: Expiry, as seconds since the Unix epoch. The comparison is inclusive: is_expired_at(now) is true when now >= exp, so a token whose exp is now is expired.

iat.description: Issued-at, as seconds since the Unix epoch.

auth_time.description: When the user actually authenticated, as seconds since the Unix epoch. Distinct from iat: a token minted an hour after authentication has a much later iat than auth_time, and that gap is exactly the signal a client needs to decide whether to ask for a step-up.

nonce.description: The nonce from the authorization request. Required whenever the request carried one — its absence from a response to a request that had one is a replay. Carried on the wire as null when the request had none, because the field has no skip_serializing_if.
nonce.x-serde-note: Option<String> with no skip_serializing_if and no default attribute, so it is serialised as null when absent.

acr.description: The authentication context class reference — this provider's assurance level. Two declared values: urn:ecoma:loa:1 for AAL1 and urn:ecoma:loa:2 for AAL2. These are this provider's OWN values, not the ISO or OIDC AAL claim values: a client matching on 'urn:ecoma:loa:1' learns the user proved one factor, and a client matching on the raw AAL string would not find one.

x-accepted-values.constraining: the field is a String in Rust

amr.description: The authentication methods used, as an array of strings. The four declared AMR values are otp (both the emailed code and a time-based one-time password), user (a passkey), and federated (a federated provider). The array may be empty; it is never omitted.

x-accepted-values.constraining: the field is a Vec<String> in Rust; the four constants collapse to three distinct wire values because the email code and the TOTP code are both 'otp'

name.description: The display name, when the 'profile' scope was granted. Absent otherwise.
name.x-serde-note: #[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")] — absent from the payload, not null.

email.description: The email address, when the 'email' scope was granted. Absent otherwise.
email.x-serde-note: #[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")] — absent from the payload, not null.

email_verified.description: Whether the address was proven. Present whenever email is. A client keying on email without reading this has an account-takeover bug.
email_verified.x-serde-note: #[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")] — absent from the payload, not null.

x-omission-rule.rule: name, email and email_verified are omitted when None; nonce is always present and may be null. The eight registered claims (iss, sub, aud, exp, iat, auth_time, acr, amr) are always present.
x-omission-rule.source: #[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")] on the three profile/email claims; no attribute on nonce
x-omission-rule.test: identity_oidc::jwt::tests::an_empty_claim_set_still_serialises_the_registered_claims asserts all eight registered claim names are present on a minimal claim set
